category_title: Academically at-risk primary students disengaged from traditional schooling but motivated by game-like virtual environments
minimal_context: The student is attending an after-school programme and is expected to complete an academic quest by submitting a digital document within a 3D virtual environment.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time to start our after-school session. Please open your assigned academic quest and begin working on your digital document submission.

STUDENT: I want to get what my classmate has. The bird on the shoulder… That one needs how many lumins?

TUTOR: We need to focus on the academic content right now. Please look at the quest.

STUDENT: Can I use genuine currency to exchange for lumins and cols in the virtual environment instead of doing this?

TUTOR: No, you have to complete the assigned work first. Go back to your document.

STUDENT: I like the 3D space as I can play with airplane, car, and boat. ... the 3D world is very fun. (Moves avatar away from the quest area to play with the yacht)

options.A: Withhold attention from the student when they engage in off-task behavior, such as playing with the yacht in the 3D virtual environment.
options.B: Sit with the student during the after-school session and discuss personal off-task topics, such as the tutor's own college basketball days.
options.C: Engage in a subtle negotiation between the amount of time spent exploring the 3D virtual environment and the amount of time spent completing the assigned academic quest.
options.D: Review the session data 20 minutes into the after-school programme and call out students who have only attempted a small portion of the academic quest.
